messages:
morgan: Heads-up — we're seeing an uptick of customer 5xxs + timeouts for hosted inference in us-west-2. Customer reports spikes in response time and some requests returning 504s.

lina: Which customer? any repro?

morgan: BrightDoc (tenant id td-341). They sent traces — gateway shows queued_request_count hitting the queue_depth_limit and continuous-batcher backlog growing. Sample log: 
```
ERROR gateway request_queue.go:217 queue_full tenant=td-341 queued=1024 max=1024 route=/v1/generate downstream_error=timeout
WARN batcher continuous_batcher.go:88 backlog=472 processing=3
```

raj: This looks like classic dequeue-starvation: batchers can't keep up, KV cache warmups + long sequences are holding slots. Is this isolated to td-341?

morgan: Right now we see a tenant-local spike but host-level queue is also at ~85% due to a few tenants having long-running streams. Metrics: p95 RT ~ 4.2s -> 12.8s for tail.

lina: customer on call is pretty unhappy, billing impact & production traffic. Can we get a short repro to confirm?

anya: Repro steps I ran locally: 1) send 40 concurrent streaming requests of ~1.5k tokens each to /v1/chat, 2) observe continuous-batcher backpressure after ~60s. I hit the queue depth limit in the gateway.

raj: Workaround options: 1) temporary routing to a less loaded region (us-east-1), 2) raise tenant queue depth for td-341, 3) enable early-reject for long seqs. Which is fastest?

morgan: Customer wants minimal impact. Suggest shifting their traffic to us-east-1 for now and we throttle long requests until we patch.

lina: I'll ask BrightDoc if they can switch region (they're using regional=us-west-2 in their config).

sre-oncall: Reassigning to me. Profiling now — capturing pprof + batcher queues. Can we up the gateway max_queue_depth from 1024 -> 1536 as a temporary emergency? Risk: memory explosion if backlog persists.

raj: If we do that, also enable tenant-level rate limit for token-length > 1000 to avoid repeat. I can push a quick config change to canary and observe.

deploy-bot: @raj started rollout: gateway-config bump max_queue_depth=1536 (canary: gw-canary-3) — 1/3 hosts updated.

morgan: Noted. Lina, any update from customer?

lina: BrightDoc said they can redirect to us-east-1 for 30m while we stabilize. They're enabling a regional fallback in-app. :relieved:

anya: After canary went up I re-ran the load repro for 3 minutes. backlog reduced from 472 -> 190 and queued requests down to ~600. p95 dropped to ~6.1s. Progress but still degraded under sustained load.

raj: We should also disable long-lived streaming from the continuous-batcher pool for a short window — move streams to a dedicated pool that doesn't block short single-request paths. I'll open a follow-up PR for pool separation.

morgan: Sounds good. For immediate mitigation: 1) BrightDoc routes to us-east-1, 2) gateway queue depth increased (canary), 3) tenant rate limit for long tokens enabled, 4) start pool-segmentation PR.

sre-oncall: Collecting logs for the window 2958879900-2958880300 and attaching to incident tracker. If the workaround holds, we'll roll the config to remaining hosts in 15m.

lina: Customer confirmed failover to us-east-1 and seeing normal latency. They will keep on east for 1h while we finish stabilization.

raj: Merged PR for tenant-long-token early-reject + metrics emit for long-seq evictions. Deploying to canary now.

deploy-bot: rollout completed: gateway-config to remaining hosts (max_queue_depth=1536) — 10/10 hosts updated.

anya: Post-rollout numbers: backlog < 50, queued < 120, p95 ~ 2.3s. No further 504s for the tenant.

morgan: Great. Action items: 
- raj: finalize pool-segmentation plan & rollout schedule.
- sre-oncall: run chaos test for queue overflow scenarios next week.
- support (lina): confirm BrightDoc can fall back automatically to multi-region in config and follow up on customer compensation if needed.

lina: I'll own follow-up and update incident. Closing this thread for now — monitoring for 1h. :white_check_mark:
